gymExerciseProgress.emptyMessage: Log this exercise 3+ times to see progress

press: Set your feet, grip just outside shoulder width and brace your core.
Lower under control until the bar or handles reach chest level, elbows at about 45°.
Press back up and stop just short of locking out, keeping shoulders down.
squat: Bar high on the back, feet shoulder width, toes turned out slightly.
Sit down between your hips until thighs pass parallel, knees tracking over toes.
Drive through mid-foot and stand tall without letting the chest drop.
hinge: Hips back, chest proud, bar close to the shins with a neutral spine.
Push the hips back until you feel the hamstrings load, bar grazing the legs.
Squeeze the glutes to stand up — the bar path stays vertical.
row: Set a stable torso angle and pull the shoulder blades down first.
Row to the lower ribs, elbows past the body, no shrugging.
Lower under control for a full stretch before the next rep.
curl: Elbows pinned to the ribs, wrists neutral, shoulders relaxed.
Curl until the forearm passes vertical without swinging the torso.
Lower slowly for three counts — the negative is the work.
raise: Slight forward lean, elbows soft, weights beside the thighs.
Lift out to shoulder height leading with the elbows, not the hands.
Pause a beat at the top, then lower under tension.
push: Stand a step back from the stack, elbows tight to your sides.
Extend to full lockout, pausing briefly with the triceps contracted.
Return only until the forearms reach parallel to keep tension.
cardio: Warm up for three to five minutes at an easy pace.
Hold each interval at its target speed — breathing hard but able to speak a word.
Finish with two minutes of walking to bring the heart rate down.
other: Set up so the working muscle is the only thing moving.
Move through the full range you can control, no bouncing.
Match last session’s numbers before adding weight.

You are responsible for the accuracy of what you enter and for keeping your account secure.

theService.heading: The service
body: Lume logs food by search, barcode, nutrition-label photograph, meal photograph, quick add, saved meals and recipes; logs gym sessions against a weekly schedule and templates; computes energy expenditure from published ACSM metabolic equations for treadmill, cycling, rowing and stair climbing, and a MET estimate elsewhere; reconciles calories in against your basal metabolic rate plus logged exercise; and generates written insights from your own logged data.
Estimates produced from a photograph are estimates. Each one carries a confidence score rather than being presented as certain.

subscriptions.heading: Subscriptions and billing
body: Lume Pro is an optional auto-renewing subscription purchased through Apple’s in-app purchase system. Payment is charged to your Apple ID, and we never receive your payment details.
New subscribers get a {{trialDays}}-day free trial.

Apple shows you the exact price, the billing period and the renewal terms before you confirm. Subscriptions renew automatically unless auto-renew is turned off at least 24 hours before the end of the current period. You can manage or cancel a subscription at any time in your Apple ID subscription settings. Refunds are handled by Apple under its own policies.

freeTier.heading: Free tier and limits
body: A free tier covers manual, search and barcode logging, nutrition-label scanning, a daily allowance of photograph scans, all gym features, your dashboards and energy balance, data export and account deletion. The app shows your current scan allowance and what remains of it.

Each is described in the Privacy Policy and is governed by its own terms. Australian food data comes from the Australian Food Composition Database (Release 3), © Food Standards Australia New Zealand, used under the FSANZ Data User Licence Agreement; it is based on Australian data, which may not be appropriate for use in other countries, and FSANZ does not endorse Lume.

scope.heading: What this policy covers
body: It will set out which products this policy applies to.

whatWeCollect.heading: Personal information we collect
body: Account: your email address and name, managed by our authentication provider.
Your name is kept only when Sign in with Apple or Google shares it; signing up with email asks for none. Your account also has a user ID created by Clerk.

Health information: your body weight, height, age and sex; your activity level and goal; your calorie and macro targets; and your body-weight history. Health information is sensitive information under the Privacy Act.
Fitness information: gym sessions and the exercises and parameters you record, your weekly schedule, and your streaks.

Content you create: food names and quantities, notes, recipes and saved foods, and photographs of meals and nutrition labels when you scan them. A photograph is sent for analysis only after you accept the AI disclosure.
Notifications: if you allow notifications, your device’s push token, so reminders can reach this device. It is removed when you sign out.

Usage: only if you turn it on. Product analytics is off by default. When it is on, Lume records a fixed list of twenty event names describing which features are used — never what you logged. No food names, no quantities, no photographs, no health values. You can turn it on or off at any time in Settings → Privacy; accepting the AI disclosure also turns it on.
Crash reports: when the app crashes, the error and where in the code it happened, without your account details or anything you logged.
Purchases: whether you hold an active subscription. Payment details are handled by Apple and never reach us.

sensitiveConsent.heading: Sensitive information and consent
body: Before your first meal photograph or AI request, Lume shows a one-time disclosure naming Google Gemini, and sends nothing until you accept. That acknowledgement is recorded on your device and on our server (so background processing also respects it), and it covers sharing with that processor (and with Anthropic only if our backup AI provider is switched on, as described below). You can withdraw it at any time in Settings → Privacy → Turn off AI processing.
The express consent mechanism required for collecting health information under Australian Privacy Principle 3.3 is being drafted; the disclosure above is narrower than that.

purposes.heading: Why we collect it
body: We use your data only to provide the service: to sign you in and manage your account, to store and display your logs, compute your calorie and macro targets, compute exercise energy expenditure, reconcile your energy balance, estimate the contents of a photographed meal, improve those estimates from your corrections, send the reminders you turn on, fix crashes, and determine your access to subscriber features.
We do not sell your personal information, and we never share health information for advertising.

disclosure.heading: Who we disclose it to
body: Always, to run the service: Clerk (sign-in — your email address, name and user ID), Supabase (database hosting — every row of your data), and RevenueCat (subscriptions — your user id and purchase status).

Only when you use the feature, and only after you accept the AI disclosure: Google Gemini receives the photograph you are scanning together with a short summary of your food preferences and recent corrections (so estimates improve for you), and a summary of your logged data — and, when you use Ask Lume, the question you type — to write the wording of insights, briefs and answers. Anthropic receives that summary instead only if we switch insight wording to our backup AI provider; this policy will say so before that happens.
Sentry receives crash reports. They are not linked to you: user details, request data and breadcrumb messages are removed before a report is sent.
PostHog receives product analytics events only when you have turned analytics on, which is off by default. Lume never links those events to a profile of you there.

When you search foods, Lume first searches its own copy of the Australian Food Composition Database (no data leaves our server for that), and the search text is also sent to Open Food Facts and, only where enabled, the USDA FoodData Central database. A scanned barcode number is sent to Open Food Facts. No account information goes with either.
Only if you connect them yourself: Strava and WHOOP. Neither is operational today.
Each processor handles data under its own terms and only to provide its part of the service.

overseas.heading: Overseas disclosure
body: It will identify the countries in which each processor stores and processes data, as Australian Privacy Principle 8 requires.

security.heading: Storage, security and retention
body: Traffic between the app and our servers is encrypted in transit. Every table enforces row-level security, so one account cannot read another account’s rows. Tokens for connected services are encrypted at rest with AES-256-GCM.

Meal and label photographs are not retained by us — the scan record keeps a quality score and the geometry derived from the image, not the image. The photograph is transmitted in full to Google Gemini to be analysed.

Your account data and everything you log are kept until you delete your account. Your device’s push token is removed when you sign out or delete your account. How long other records are kept after you stop using Lume is still being decided and will be stated here.

accessCorrection.heading: Access and correction
body: You can export everything we hold about you from Settings, as a single machine-readable file, and you can view and correct your profile, goals and every logged entry in the app at any time.

deletion.heading: Deleting your account
body: Deleting your account from Settings → Delete my account is immediate and destructive. Your sign-in identity is deleted first, so the account can no longer be signed into, then your data is deleted and every related record goes with it. There is no grace period.
If the identity deletion fails, the operation stops and reports an error without deleting your data — we never report a deletion that did not happen.

complaints.heading: Complaints
body: It will set out how to complain about a privacy breach, the timeframe for a response, and the escalation path to the Office of the Australian Information Commissioner.

analytics.heading: Cookies and analytics
body: Product analytics is off by default. If you turn it on in Settings → Privacy, Lume sends usage events to its own servers and to PostHog. These events never include what you logged. There are no advertising or third-party tracking SDKs in the app.
When analytics is off, nothing is collected, and turning it off discards any events not yet sent.

children.heading: Children
body: A minimum age and how it is enforced are still being decided.

contact.heading: Contact
body: A dedicated privacy contact will be published here. Until then, reach us through Settings → Help and feedback or at https://lume.fit/support.
